developer: Keep components thin: template bindings and event handlers only; fetching, mapping and business rules live in injectable services.
Inject with the constructor or `inject()`; never `new` a service. Check `providedIn` and module providers before adding a provider.
Subscriptions must end: prefer the `async` pipe, `takeUntilDestroyed`, or `take(1)`; no manual `subscribe` without teardown.
Follow the repo state pattern (NgRx or services with RxJS): changes go through actions/reducers or the service, never by mutating state in a component.
Touching a component means checking its template, its `selector` users and its routes: the impact lookup shows template-uses and route couplings.
Use typed forms and strict templates; no `any` in new code; keep `ChangeDetectionStrategy` consistent with neighbours.
tester: Unit tests sit next to the file as `*.spec.ts` and use the existing TestBed setup; reuse the repo's test helpers and mock services.
Test behaviour through the rendered template and public methods, not private members; assert emitted outputs and called service methods.
Async code: use `fakeAsync`/`tick` or `waitForAsync`; flag tests that depend on real timers or the network.
For NgRx: test reducers as pure functions, selectors with sample state, effects with marbles or `of`.
Check the Karma/Jasmine config runs headless in CI and that `fdescribe`/`fit` was not committed.
security: No `bypassSecurityTrust*` and no `innerHTML` binding on values that can contain user input.
Tokens and personal data do not belong in `localStorage`, URLs or logs; check interceptors attach credentials only to your own API origins.
Route guards and resolvers must enforce authorization server-side too; a hidden menu item is not access control.
Environment files: only public values; secrets never ship in the bundle. Check `src/environments` changes carefully.
Third-party scripts, iframes and `window.open` need an allow-list and `noopener`.
peer-review: Does the template still match the component API (inputs, outputs, selectors) after the change? Open the templates that use it.
Lazy-loaded modules, route data and guards: does any route now point at something renamed or removed?
Change detection and performance: new `ngFor` without `trackBy`, heavy work in getters, subscriptions in loops.
Duplicated pipes, directives or services that already exist in `shared/` or `core/`.
Accessibility basics on new UI: labels, focus order, keyboard use, contrast.
auditor: Rules that name Angular files should use the `name.kind.ts` suffixes seen in the repo; test-location rules should say `*.spec.ts` next to the source.
